messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Perceived depression scores improved significantly more in the TRI 360TM multi-ingredient supplement group than in the placebo group.
Sentence: "All assessed perception scorings on psychological symptoms like fatigue, mental stress, sleep disturbance, anxiety, depression, emotional trauma, mood changes, self-confidence, willpower, and motivation were very significantly (p ≤ 0.0001) improved in TRI 360TM participants than placebo control group."
Measured as: depression perception scoring
Population: Adults aged 20-45 years with one or more psychological symptoms
Intervention: TRI 360TM proprietary nutraceutical combination capsules twice a day, up to 180 days
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 84
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Mid-life serum 25(OH)D concentrations were not significantly associated with depressive symptoms 20 years later.
Sentence: "There was no significant association with functional ability or depressive symptoms."
Measured as: depressive symptoms
Population: 13,039 white and black ARIC participants, mean age 57 at mid-life, 57% women, 24% black
Intervention: Mid-life serum 25(OH)D concentration (observational exposure, visit 2)
Comparator: Higher vs lower 25(OH)D categories (deficient <20, intermediate 20-<30, sufficient >=30 ng/mL)
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 13,039
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A tests a proprietary multi-ingredient supplement (not stated to include vitamin D) with a perception score for depression, while Study B is a cohort on serum 25(OH)D; the conflict hinges on whether A's exposure is vitamin D at all, and nothing shown makes it a vitamin D comparison.","verdict":"off_question","reason":null,"also_differs":[],"detail":"exposure: TRI 360TM multi-ingredient nutraceutical, vitamin D not identified as a component"}
